subject: general
question: A sum of money triples itself at a certain rate of compound interest in 3 years. In how many years will it amount to 27 times of itself?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Under **Compound Interest**, if a sum becomes **n** times in **t** years, it will become **nx** times in **x × t** years.

Given: Money becomes **3 times** (3¹) in **3 years**.

Required: Money to become **27 times** (which is 3³) of itself.

Here, n = 3, t = 3, and x = 3 (since 27 = 3³).

⇒ Total time = x × t = 3 × 3 = **9 years**.

**∴ The correct answer is 9 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Sum triples in 3 years.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b6fefa85d434765b6839214415103ce514d19e625719118167e3297e430a1d20.png] 

Let the **Principal** be P and the **Rate of Interest** be r% per annum.

Using **Compound Interest** formula: A = P(1 + r/100)t

⇒ 3P = P(1 + r/100)³

⇒ 3 = (1 + r/100)³ ... (i)

For the sum to become 27 times, let the time be **n** years:

⇒ 27P = P(1 + r/100)ⁿ

⇒ 27 = (1 + r/100)ⁿ

⇒ (3)³ = (1 + r/100)ⁿ

Substitute the value of 3 from equation (i):

⇒ [(1 + r/100)³]³ = (1 + r/100)ⁿ

⇒ (1 + r/100)⁹ = (1 + r/100)ⁿ

⇒ n = **9 years**.

**∴ The correct answer is 9 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Standard CI Formula

The amount A is calculated as A = P(1 + r/n)ⁿt, where n is the number of times interest is compounded per year.

Simple Interest vs Compound Interest

In SI, the principal remains constant, so growth is linear. In CI, interest is added to the principal, leading to exponential growth.

Rule of 72

A quick way to estimate the doubling time of an investment is t ≈ 72 ÷ r, where r is the annual interest rate.</p
